ai_show_review.summary: Epic Mountains‑Moon > Dark Star suite with soaring solos and tight rhythm
ai_show_review.blurb: The show shines on the massive Mountains Of The Moon → Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven sequence, backed by powerful organ work and crisp drum interplay. Jerry’s guitar soars while Phil locks down the pocket; the set is a high‑energy, cohesive journey from start to finish.
ai_show_review.review: April 22, 1969 at Boston’s Ark captures the Dead in top form. The first set rolls out with a bright “Sitting On Top Of The World” and an emotive “Morning Dew,” but it’s the second set that cements this night’s legend. A blistering “Dupree's Diamond Blues” launches into an uninterrupted arc of “Mountains Of The Moon → Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven,” a suite reviewers call "epic" and "genius," where Garcia’s guitar rides massive analog feedback and Tom Constanten’s organ fills the mix with depth. Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart provide tight, stereo‑placed drumming that drives the improvisations, while Phil Lesh holds down a thunderous bass line through The Eleven. Despite occasional tape‑flip glitches, both soundboard recordings are praised as clear, balanced masterpieces, making this show a must‑listen for anyone chasing classic late‑’60s Dead magic.

best_recording.reason: The Miller soundboard capture is the most complete and balanced, offering clear overall sound despite minor tape‑flip glitches.

key_highlights: Monumental Mountains Of The Moon → Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven suite
Tom Constanten’s organ adds depth and balances Pigpen’s harmonica rap moments
Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart deliver tight, stereo‑placed drumming throughout
Strong performances of Dupree's Diamond Blues, Morning Dew, and Sitting On Top Of The World
song_highlights: Sitting On Top Of The World

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar soars with massive analog feedback and genius solos, especially during Dark Star and the Mountains Of The Moon jam.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a monster bass line that locks into the pocket on The Eleven and adds solid vocal harmonies.
band_performance.Bob: Weir sits low in the mix on The Eleven but keeps steady rhythm guitar and contributes reliable vocal harmony throughout.
band_performance.Brent: Tom Constanten’s organ is prominent and well‑balanced, adding depth to the jams; Pigpen’s harmonica and brief “pig rap” add flavor.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart delivers tight, driving drumming with excellent stereo placement, crucial to the momentum of The Eleven and Dark Star.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann supplies powerful drum rolls around the 24‑25 minute mark of Dark Star, intensifying the improvisational peak.

must_listen_sequences: Sitting On Top Of The World
